articles.title: World Central Kitchen founder says three killed in Gaza strike 'not part of our team'
articles.summary:
World Central Kitchen founder says three killed in Gaza strike 'not part of our team'

The founder of the World Central Kitchen, Jose Andres, has said that the three people killed in an Israeli strike on a vehicle delivering food aid in Gaza, did not belong the organisation, nor did the vehicle.

In a post on X, Andres said, "Early reports linked them to World Central Kitchen. They were not part of our team, and it was not our vehicle. That's all we know."

"But here is what I do know. More than a year into a ceasefire, people in Gaza are still dying. Families are facing a fourth winter in tents," he added.

The Israeli army had earlier claimed in a post on X that it targeted three “Islamic Jihad terrorists” in a vehicle used to transport food and supplies to other group operatives in Gaza.

Andres added that a "ceasefire is not peace", calling upon leaders to work towards ending the conflict.

"To every leader with the power to change this, on every side: finish the work. End this war for good, so Palestinians and Israelis can live in safety, and so the people of Gaza can start to rebuild their homes, their schools, their kitchens," he said.

"Our teams, Gazans feeding Gazans, were cooking again today. They will be there tomorrow. A plate of food is hope. But it is not a future. Peace is."

articles.title: Pro-Israel Hakeem Jeffries says he will push legislation targeting settler violence
articles.summary:
Pro-Israel Hakeem Jeffries says he will push legislation targeting settler violence

Pro-Israel US Democratic leader, Hakeem Jeffries, who is expected to become the first Black speaker of the House of Representatives next year, has pledged to advance legislation targeting Israeli settler violence in the occupied West Bank within the first 100 days of the new Congress.

In an interview with The New York Times, Jeffries said the West Bank Settler Violence Protection and Prevention Act should be among the early legislative priorities, adding that he expected strong support for it within the House Democratic Caucus.

Jeffries also described the devastation inflicted on Palestinian civilians in Gaza as “unacceptable, unsustainable and un-American”, calling for increased humanitarian assistance, medical aid, housing support and access to clean water and air.

Asked whether he supported the proposed Block the Bombs and Stop the Settlements bills, which call for restricting arms sale to Israel and broader sanctions on settlement expansion, Jeffries said he had not taken a position.

On calls to halt US weapons exports used in regional conflicts, he said the current approach was “not sustainable” and needed to change.

More than a million people have signed a petition urging Democrats to reject Hakeem Jeffries as the next Speaker of the US House of Representative. An Economist/YouGov poll published last month found that Jeffries had just a 26 percent approval rating among registered voters. 

Critics say that one reason Jeffries' popularity has taken a hit is that he is an avid supporter of Israel.

The American Israel Public Affairs Committee (Aipac) ranks among his top campaign-financing contributors.

articles.title: Former UN envoy says Iran war was 'perfectly avoidable'
articles.summary:
Former UN envoy says Iran war was 'perfectly avoidable'

Iran war could have been avoided, Álvaro de Soto, a former UN special coordinator for the Middle East peace process, has said.

“It was perfectly avoidable. It need not have happened,” he said, adding that US officials have offered differing explanations for going to war.

Speaking at MED Dialogues conference in Naples, he said: “Lasting peace requires a willingness to confront the problems at the root of a conflict. Without addressing them, opportunities for peace will continue to be missed.”

articles.summary: Six Palestinians, including a child and a woman, were wounded in Israeli attacks across the Gaza Strip on Saturday, according to medical sources, Anadolu reports.
